game: PIT@TB Week 6 / kickoff not in pack / TB +2.5 (PIT -2.5) / total 38 / implied PIT 20.25 TB 17.75 / weather not saved / outdoor venue assumed, rest-travel and line movement not in pack

script.base: Market prices a one-score grind, not a shootout: PIT slight favorite, both implied totals in the high teens/low 20s. PIT leads by a FG late. Both lean run — Warren has been 16.3 carries/game (49/321 L3) and Irving 17.3 (52/272 L3). TB's 41% blitz meets a Rodgers unit at -0.38 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=52), so PIT throws short; TB does not have to abandon Irving because the game stays inside one score.
script.flip1: PIT jumps ahead by 10+ early, clocks out with Warren, and TB abandons the run. Irving's carry share dies (the KC-style underdog flip) while Egbuka (22 tgt L3), Otton (16) and Godwin (14) absorb the pass volume.
script.flip2: TB hangs around or leads and both QBs stay pressured (TB QB -0.21 EPA vs blitz, n=71; PIT only blitzes 27%). Explosives stall — TB has allowed just 14 passes of 20+ on 173 att, PIT 19/169 — and the 38 total sags into a short-throw, two-back slog.

injury_fallout: No injury report, practice trend, questionable tags, or inactives in the pack — final-inactive checkpoint cannot be run. Usage proxy only: PIT backfield is Warren (49 carries, 17 targets L3); Homer 3/-1, Rodgers 3/18 rush, Nichols 2/6; Rico Dowdle is on the board (rush 18, rec 7, rush+rec 26.5) but has zero listed L3 carries, so any Dowdle activation is an unconfirmed Warren risk, not a confirmed split. TB rush committee is Irving 52/272, Daniels 14/89, Gainwell 10/19, Tucker 8/28 — Irving is the share, not a monopoly. No OL or coverage-player absences are listed, so pressure and run-fit reads use season rates only.

matchup.shell: Coverage shell not charted (no MOFO/MOFC or man/zone rate in pack). Proxy: TB location splits — middle 9.25 YPA on only 32 att vs left 6.59 (78 att) and right 6.48 (56 att). PIT is flat: left 7.35 (77), middle 7.27 (33), right 7.54 (48).
matchup.pressure: TB blitzes 41%; Rodgers is -0.38 EPA/dropback vs blitz vs -0.01 with no blitz, so pressure should cut deep shots and force checkdowns. PIT blitzes only 27%; TB QB is -0.21 vs blitz and -0.10 without, a smaller gap.
matchup.bleeds: TB run fit is the stingy side: 3.61 YPC allowed, only 9 runs of 10+ in 5 games, and few explosives (14/173). Their pass bleed is the middle, not the outside. PIT run defense is the soft spot: 4.21 YPC, 13 runs of 10+, and a higher explosive-pass rate (19/169) with no location hole.
matchup.overlap: Irving's carry share (52 of the listed TB rushes L3) runs into the defense that actually gives up rushing. Warren is PIT's checkdown (17 targets, -21 air yards, 169 rec yds L3), which is exactly what a 41% blitz against a blitz-allergic QB produces. Metcalf (18 tgt, 243 air, 13.5 aDOT) attacks the outside/deep area TB has not bled (6.5 YPA, 14 explosives). Freiermuth has the air (160) but only 91 yards — middle volume without the catch efficiency.

form: Avoiding season averages. Irving L3: 52/272 rush (5.23 YPC, 90.7/g) plus only 7 targets/22 rec yds — rush role is stable, receiving is a crumb (7.3 yds/g). Daniels 29.7 rush yds/g on 4.7 carries sits under a 33.5 line but is a vulture, not the story. Warren L3 rush 107.0/g at 6.55 YPC is the fluky piece vs a 3.61 YPC defense; his receiving 56.3/g on 5.7 targets is YAC-heavy (-21 air) so the 56 will not repeat, but 5-6 YPT on that target count still clears 27.5. Metcalf 52.7 rec yds/g vs a 50.5 line is a push. Otton 39.3/g on 16 targets vs 27.5 is real volume but PIT has no middle bleed to upgrade it. Egbuka 37.7 vs a 37 line is a coin flip (5.1 YPT on 180 air). Godwin 31.0 vs 26.5, low aDOT (37 air/14 tgt). Hurst 21.7 on only 6 targets is spike-prone (Johnson 89 yds on 5 targets looks like one play). No similar-defense game splits in the pack.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Irving is the TB carry share (17.3/g, 5.23 YPC L3) against the soft side of this defense — PIT allows 4.21 YPC and 13 runs of 10+ — in a one-score game that does not force Tampa off the run.
edge_players.must_be_true: Game stays within one score so TB does not abandon the run; Irving keeps the L3 share (~15+ carries) rather than a Daniels/Gainwell/Tucker split; no unlisted OL or Irving inactive.
edge_players.kills_it: PIT leads by 10+ early and Irving drops under ~12 carries, or the committee (Daniels already 14 carries L3) steals the rushing downs in a grind.

edge_players.edge_sentence: TB will blitz (41%) a QB who collapses when blitzed (-0.38 EPA), and Warren is already the checkdown (17 targets, -21 air yards L3), so the 27.5 rec-yard line is behind the role even if the 56-yard YAC average regresses.
edge_players.must_be_true: Warren keeps passing-down snaps (Dowdle not stealing them — Dowdle had no listed L3 carries); Rodgers checks down instead of only taking sacks; at least ~5 targets at a modest YPT.
edge_players.kills_it: PIT pure clock-kill with Warren at 1-2 targets, Dowdle taking third-down work, or the -21 air-yard YAC spike was two plays and he finishes around 12 yards.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack — cannot size to a model or test the 70% calibration warning. Available form agrees with both reads and does not contradict them: Irving 90.7 rush yds/g vs 64.5; even a regression to PIT's 4.21 YPC on 16 carries is ~67, still over. Warren rec 56.3/g vs 27.5 is inflated by YAC, but 5.7 targets times a regressed 5-6 YPT still lands ~29-34, so the low rung survives the fluky-yards flag. Not cutting either. Prices: Irving rush over 64.5 is -113; Warren rec over 27.5 is +nan (unpriced). Do not treat this as a 70%+ ticket.

market_rung_price: Volume/carry-share market, main rung only: buckyirving rushyds OVER 64.5 at -113 (not the rushrec 79.5, which needs ~15 rec yards he has not produced — 22 rec yds total L3). Role/checkdown market: jaylenwarren recyds OVER 27.5, price missing (+nan). No alt rungs. Pass Metcalf under 50.5 (52.7 L3, number is the average), Freiermuth 33.5 (30.3 L3 but middle is TB's only pass bleed), Otton over 27.5 (form only, no PIT location hole), Dowdle anything (no L3 role).
pre_mortem: It's Monday and Irving under 64.5 lost the ticket because PIT scored on the first two drives, TB was in pass-mode by the second quarter, and Daniels plus Gainwell took the remaining rushing downs — 52 carries L3 was never a lock on script. Warren under 27.5 lost the other leg because the blitz turned into sacks rather than checkdowns (the -0.38 EPA) and Dowdle, who was already on the prop board, took the third-down snaps, leaving Warren as a pure runner against a 3.61 YPC defense. That counter-case is real but narrower than the base one-score script, so the legs stay, tagged to those kills.
slip_story: One story only: low-total competitive grind (38, PIT -2.5). Stack Irving rush over with Warren checkdown rec over — both win if the game stays close, TB runs, and PIT's blitz-forced throws stay short. Do not add Metcalf/Egbuka/Godwin overs, a total over, or Irving rush under. Warren rush under 60.5 is the opposite script piece (needs efficiency collapse despite favorite clock-kill volume) and stays off the slip. No TDs, no receptions, no passing yards.
